current_activity: CMH table date for Third Army attachment (alternate to the Green Book date of 20 December)
notes: Event date: 17 December 1944 (CMH ETO order-of-battle table for the 101st Airborne Division: VIII Corps, First Allied Airborne Army assigned, Third Army attached and 12th Army Group attached, all from 17 December). Event definition: this row is the date the CMH table gives for the division's corps and Third Army attachment; the Green Book places the division on the road from Camp Mourmelon on the night of 18 December (Ardennes p308) and VIII Corps' transfer to Third Army on 20 December (p399), so the table date is an administrative date, not the date command was exercised. Event definition: conflict with the 20 December row (G016): same relationship (Third Army attached), different date. The Green Book row is preferred because it is a dated narrative about the transfer; the table row is kept as an alternate. Relationship: VIII Corps unspecified_subordination, First Allied Airborne Army assigned, Third Army attached and 12th Army Group attached, all from 17 December (CMH table). Location: Camp Mourmelon (Mourmelon-le-Grand): the atlas lists the division there on 1 December and the Green Book has it moving from Camp Mourmelon to Bastogne on 18 December; no source places it elsewhere on 17 December. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Mourmelon-le-Grand. Event support: low (a table date contradicted by a narrative page). Location support: low (an inference from the departure on the 18th; the atlas entry is 16 days earlier).

notes: Event date: 19 December 1944 (Ardennes p308: the move from Camp Mourmelon to Bastogne, 107 miles, with the 501st detrucking at midnight; "By 0900 on 19 December McAuliffe had all four regiments in hand"). Event definition: the 101st Airborne Division, held in SHAEF reserve at Mourmelon, is committed to the VIII Corps at Bastogne; this is the division's arrival at the town, not the encirclement (21 December). Relationship: VIII Corps (CMH table, from 17 December; the Green Book has the corps under First Army until 20 December) and First Allied Airborne Army assigned. The CMH table lists Third Army attached from 17 December, which conflicts with Ardennes p399 (VIII Corps to Third Army during the 20th); that entry is left to the 20 December row. Location: Bastogne town centroid; the atlas lists the division at Bastogne on 19 December. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Bastogne. Event support: high (Green Book and atlas agree). Location support: high for the date and place (a division command post in the town). Command support: the corps entry date is from the CMH table; the Green Book places the division in Bastogne on 18-19 December.

current_activity: passes with VIII Corps from First Army to Third Army
notes: Event date: 20 December 1944 (Ardennes p399: "The VIII Corps passed to General Patton's Third Army during the 20th", with some confusion in the units attached to the corps as to their exact status; the CMH table dates the Third Army attachment from 17 December, three days earlier, before the division reached Bastogne). Event definition: who controls the division at noon on 20 December: VIII Corps, under First Army until the corps passed to Third Army sometime that day; the dataset records Third Army from 20 December as the Green Book states it and does not choose an hour. The CMH table's 17 December date is retained in the entry note and not used. Relationship: VIII Corps; Third Army from 20 December (Green Book) against 17 December (CMH table): a documented disagreement; First Allied Airborne Army assigned; 12th Army Group attached through Third Army. Location: Bastogne, the division command post (atlas 19 December; Ardennes p456 for 20 December planning at Bastogne). Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Bastogne. Event support: moderate (the day is documented, the hour and the table date are not reconciled). Location support: high (command post at Bastogne for the day).

current_activity: Bastogne is surrounded; the division holds a perimeter around the town
notes: Event date: 21 December 1944 (Ardennes p458: "by daylight on the 21st the German infantry following the armored troops were ensconced on both the main roads running from Bastogne south", while in the north the circle had been clamped shut during the preceding hours). Event definition: the road net around Bastogne is cut and the 101st Airborne (with attached armor and the VIII Corps remnants) is encircled; the row dates the first full day of the encirclement, not the German first contact on the 20th. Relationship: VIII Corps and Third Army (see the 20 December row). Location: The atlas lists the division command post at Bastogne on 19 December and nothing else for the siege; no source places the command post anywhere but the town until the relief.
